title: BLOOD DRIVE TODAY
full_story:
Clay County residents have an opportunity to help save lives before Thanksgiving.

The American Red Cross is teaming up with the Flora Chamber Of Commerce and Flora Odd Fellows Lodge number 151 for a blood drive today from 1:00 to 5:00 pm at the Flora Odd Fellows Lodge, located at 231 East North Avenue in Flora.

Organizers note that the winter holidays often bring a drop in donations, making local drives essential for maintaining area blood supplies.  As an added incentive, those who come out to give blood on Wednesday will receive an exclusive American Red Cross and Wheel Of Fortune mug, while supplies last.

To donate, individuals must be at least 17 years old, weigh at least 110 pounds, and be in generally good health.  Donors are asked to bring a blood donor card, driver’s license, or two other forms of identification.

Appointments can be made using the Red Cross Blood Donor App, by visiting RedCrossBlood.org, by calling 1-800-RED CROSS or by enabling the Blood Donor Skill on Alexa Echo devices.  Donors can use RapidPass online on the day of their appointment to complete pre-donation reading and health history questionnaires before arriving.

The next Blood Drive in our area will be on Tuesday, December 1st from Noon to 6 pm at the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church in the Link Gymnasium.  The next Blood Drive at the Flora Church of the Nazarene will be on Thursday, December 10th from Noon to 5 pm.

title: EFFINGHAM MAN ARRESTED
full_story:
An Effingham man is facing preliminary battery and firearms charges following an alleged altercation in rural Rinard.

Wayne County Sheriff Chris Otey says 21-year-old Carson L. Chasteen was arrested after allegedly punching his girlfriend’s uncle multiple times during a dispute on Friday.  Authorities say the victim, who is over 60 years old, required medical attention for his injuries.

Deputies say Chasteen also fired several gunshots into the air during the incident, though no one was struck by the gunfire.

Chasteen was booked into the Wayne County Jail.  The incident remains under investigation.

title: WAYNE COUNTY RACCOON ROUNDUP
full_story:
The Wayne County Farm Bureau is having a Raccoon Round-up on December 8th from 6 to 7 pm and then again on January 19th from 6 to 7 pm.

The initiative offers a $3 cash reward per raccoon tail for Farm Bureau members during the Illinois hunting and trapping season.  Participants are limited to 33 tails per collection date and must present a valid DNR hunting or trapping license.  All harvests must strictly follow state regulations.

The Clay County Farm Bureau is also having a “Raccoon Roundup” to combat rising property damage from an increased raccoon population.  The next collection event will take place at the Farm Bureau office in Louisville from 6:00 to 7:00 PM on Thursday, January 14th.

title: OCC CHRISTMAS CONCERT
full_story:
The Olney Central College Community Choir will present its annual Christmas Concert at 7 pm on December 3rd in the Dr. John D. Stull Performing Arts Center.

Director of Choral Activities Dr. Andrew Pittman said this year’s concert will feature a variety of music, blending year-round favorites with holiday selections.

Bringing those pieces to life is a group of 28 singers, representing a mix of high school and college students along with seasoned veterans.

“We’re glad to see so many new faces this semester,” Pittman added.  “One of the joys of making music is bringing people of all ages together.  We’re excited to share that joy this season.”

As Route 66 celebrates its 100th anniversary, the choir will pay tribute to the historic Mother Road with a performance of (Get Your Kicks on) Route 66, the popular 1946 hit written by American songwriter Bobby Troup.  Established on November 11th, 1926, Route 66 was one of the nation’s first numbered highways, connecting Chicago to Los Angeles across 2,448 miles and eight states.  Adding a personal connection to the celebration, Pittman noted choir member Jack Eyer traveled the entire length of Route 66 earlier this year.

Other selections will include Colors of the Wind, written by composer Alan Menken and lyricist Stephen Schwartz for the 1995 Disney animated film Pocahontas; Leonard Cohen’s hauntingly beautiful Hallelujah; and George Frideric Handel’s Sing Out Your Joy to God, an uplifting, Baroque-inspired sacred choral anthem.

The choir will swing into the holiday season with Gettin’ in the Mood (for Christmas), Brian Setzer’s festive take on the Glenn Miller classic.  Setzer, best known as the frontman of the Stray Cats, gives the arrangement a lively, swing-inspired sound.

Among Pittman’s favorite selections for the concert is Roger Emerson’s medley arrangement pairing Christmas Time Is Here, from A Charlie Brown Christmas, with Pure Imagination, from Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory.

“It is surprisingly lovely,” Pittman said.  “I’m really impressed with what he did with this piece.”

The choir will turn to a more traditional celebration of the season with All the Earth Rejoice with a Gladsome Voice, a sacred choral arrangement featuring music by Baroque composer Antonio Vivaldi.

Following a long-standing tradition, the concert will conclude with a Christmas carol sing-along.

“We have a great variety of music this year and we hope everyone will come out and join us,” Pittman added.

Admission to the concert is free.  Donations will be accepted to support the OCC Music Department.

title: LANES REOPENING
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation announced that lanes that have been closed for construction will reopen, where possible, for the long Thanksgiving holiday weekend to minimize travel disruption.

Non-emergency closures will be suspended from 3 pm today, through 11:59 pm Sunday.

The following work zones with lane closures will remain in place during the holiday weekend.  In Richland County, Illinois 130 over the East Fork Fox River about a mile north of Olney; lane reductions continue with traffic controlled by temporary signals.  And in Marion County, Old US 51 over Crooked Creek near Central City; closed.

The public can expect delays and should allow extra time for trips through these areas.  Drivers are urged to pay close attention to changed conditions and signs in the work zones, obey the posted speed limits, refrain from using mobile devices and stay alert for workers and equipment.  At all times, please buckle up and drive sober.

For more information or to view area construction details, check the traveler information map on GettingAroundIllinois.com.

title: EXTENDED SPRING TURKEY HUNTING
full_story:
Spring turkey hunters in Illinois will have additional time to hunt on eligible private and federal lands each day of the season starting in 2027, offering more flexibility to plan around work, school and family schedules.

Legal hunting hours will be extended to one-half hour before sunrise until sunset, except on Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR)-owned, managed or leased sites and US Army Corps of Engineers-owned sites where hunting will continue to end at 1 pm.  Hunters must follow applicable site rules and access restrictions.

The change applies to both the regular spring turkey season and the youth spring turkey season.  Hunters should confirm the ownership and management of the property they plan to hunt, particularly where federal, state, and private lands meet.  Existing permit requirements, season segments and harvest limits continue to apply.

“IDNR is pleased to offer adult and youth hunters more flexibility and opportunity to get in the field during Illinois’ popular spring turkey season,” IDNR Director Jim Montgomery said.  “Our goal is to boost hunter participation, and we know that work and school obligations can be barriers to the activity.  By offering all-day turkey hunting, we hope to reduce those barriers.”

“Given that more than 95% of land in Illinois is privately owned and we know from hunter surveys that lack of time is a challenge, expanding hunting hours provides greater opportunity for turkey hunters to enjoy time in the field,” said IDNR wild turkey program manager Luke Garver.  “We have considered the sound research and the experiences of other states that offer this opportunity, and we believe that Illinois’ robust turkey population can accommodate this change.”

“When turkey seasons were first initiated, less was known about the impact of hunting on turkey populations and most Midwestern states took a conservative approach to what was allowed, including daily midday season closures.  As technology has expanded and decades of trend data and modeling provide better information, managers can fine tune season structure to allow more opportunity without any negative impacts to the population,” said John Burk, regional biologist with the National Wild Turkey Federation.  “We fully support the decision of IDNR to make the adjustment to all day turkey hunting that is in perfect alignment with the second half of our mission: the preservation of the hunting heritage.”

The first lottery for the spring turkey season closes December 1st for Illinois residents only.  Additional information is available online.  Hunters should review current harvest-reporting instructions and location-specific requirements before hunting.

The printed 2026-2027 Hunting and Trapping Digest lists the previous spring hunting hours because the change had not been approved before the publication deadline.  Hunters should consult updated IDNR information and the rules for their hunting location before going afield.

title: THANKSGIVING GAS TAX
full_story:
Those traveling by car in Illinois for Thanksgiving will pay the second-highest gas taxes in the country.

And despite Pritzker’s suspension of the automatic, inflation-linked increase in the state gas tax, Illinois’ gas taxes still total more than last year because of the statewide prepaid sales tax rate of 6.25% on the base price of gasoline.  That tax has increased as gas prices have surged across the country.

The average gas price in Illinois was $3.88 a gallon on November 23rd, according to AAA, up from $3.29 a year ago.  Federal and state taxes account for 88.8 cents of that; 36 cents higher than the national average.

Illinois’ high gas taxes are a relatively recent phenomenon.  The state gas tax had been 19 cents a gallon since 1990, but it doubled in 2019 when Gov. JB Pritzker signed the Rebuild Illinois legislation, which also allows for automatic increases every July based on inflation.  The Illinois state gas tax is now 48.3 cents a gallon.  The federal tax has been 18.4 cents since 1993.

Drivers got some relief this year, as the fiscal 2027 Illinois budget suspended the planned 1.3-cent increase until the beginning of next year.  But despite this freeze, Illinoisans still pay more in taxes than they did a year ago because of the additional 6.25% statewide sales tax on the base price of gasoline.  As prices have gone up, so has the tax paid ger gallon.

Starting in July, the state’s prepaid sales tax rate on gas rose from 17 cents a gallon to 21 cents.  So despite the rhetoric around the freeze in the state Motor Fuels Tax increase, Illinois drivers are paying 4 cents more per gallon in state tax than they were a year ago.

Chicago’s total gas tax is even higher.  The city charges a 10.50% sales tax rate, which increased slightly in August for the new Northern Illinois Transit Authority, formerly known as the Regional Transportation Authority.  Chicago residents also pay 6 cents per gallon imposed by Cook County and 8 cents by the city.  That makes their total gas tax bill up to $1.17 per gallon and explains a large part of why gas in the city averaged $4.39 per gallon on November 23rd, according to AAA.

title: CARLYLE LAKE SEEKING INTERNS
full_story:
The US Army Corps of Engineers Carlyle Lake Project is gearing up to hire interns for the 2027 summer recreation season.

Officials are hosting an Internship Open House at the Carlyle Lake Visitor Center on Friday, November 27th, at 11 am.  The event will cover job expectations, application steps, and the differences between the Pathways Internship and Student Conservation Association programs.  Current staff will also be on hand to answer questions and talk about their work.

Summer interns help visitors, lead interpretive programs, maintain recreation areas, and assist with environmental projects.

Applicants must be at least 18 years old by the start date, hold a high school diploma or G-E-D by May 31st, 2027, and be enrolled or accepted into a qualifying college, university, or technical school.  Candidates also need at least a 2.0 GPA and must be available to work a full-time, 40-hour schedule that includes weekends and holidays.

For more information, contact the Carlyle Lake Project Office at (618) 594-2484, ext. 3, or email [email protected].

title: STATE BUYS BONDS
full_story:
Illinois State Treasurer Michael Frerichs announced his office purchased $50 million in Republic of Poland Bonds.

“These bonds provide a strong investment for the people of Illinois,” Treasurer Frerichs said during a news conference at the Polish National Alliance headquarters in Chicago.  “Illinois has a unique relationship with Poland.  Chicago and the suburbs are home to one of the largest Polish populations in the world.  Our ties with Poland are strong, especially through trade, culture, and sister-city relationships.”

Treasurer Frerichs purchased Republic of Poland Bonds to diversify the state’s portfolio and achieve stable returns from a strong investment.  The investment involves two purchases.  One is for $25 million for four years at 4.875 percent, and the second is for $25 million for five years at a 4.625 percent.  This outpaces a US Treasury Note by about 46 basis points and will earn $250,000 more for the state.

The $50 million purchase is in addition to a $15 million purchase in March 2025, bringing the total investment with the Republic of Poland to $65 million.

The Illinois General Assembly approved a law establishing benchmarks that must be met for the state to purchase foreign bonds.  One of the benchmarks is that a nation must meet its bond payment obligations for at least 25 years, which the Republic of Poland has done.  Additionally, State Treasurer’s Office guidelines require the bonds to be rated in the three highest classifications of at least two rating services.

Also Thursday, the Illinois State Treasurer’s Office announced that it has renewed $10 million in Israel Bonds.  The five-year renewal came at an interest rate of 6.17 percent, the highest in the last 25 years.  The rate outpaces the US Treasury Note by about 124 basis points (1.24%) and will earn $620,000 more for the state compared to five-year US Treasuries.

“Every investment we make must serve the people of Illinois.  As Treasurer, my responsibility is to protect taxpayers’ money, maintain a stable and diversified portfolio, and earn the best returns possible in accordance with state law.  Those returns help grow public funds that can support the services Illinois families rely on,” Frerichs said.

“Our decision was based on an assessment of the bonds as a stable, safe and high-performing investment.  Israel Bonds have consistently generated among the highest returns in the state portfolio for two decades,” he added.

Israel has never defaulted on an interest or principal payment, so it is considered a stable and safe investment.

The state portfolio now has $90 million invested in Israel Bonds and $65 million in Republic of Poland Bonds.  The $155 million in foreign bond investments represents 0.3965 percent of the $41.6 billion state portfolio.

Investment decisions are based on multiple factors: the rate of return, the stability or safety of the investment, and cash flow needs for liquidity, all while seeking to diversify the state portfolio to mitigate credit and market risk.
